purpose: Lessons learned and exact working pipeline for rendering 1080x1920 3D WebGL (Three.js + HyperFrames) videos in Google Cloud Run / AI Studio managed sandboxes.

environment.gpu: None (software WebGL only via Chrome Headless Shell + SwiftShader)
environment.critical_timeout_rule: Never let a bash command hit the 300s timeout; an upstream deadline_exceeded can restart the container and wipe unsnapshotted state. Always wrap long renders with `timeout 240 ...`.
environment.scratch_vs_persistent: /tmp is ephemeral tmpfs; store intermediate render chunks under /workspace/<project>/parts/ and clean up after final mux.

required_markup.root: <div id="root" data-composition-id="main" data-start="0" data-duration="<sec>" data-width="1080" data-height="1920">
required_markup.canvas: <canvas id="scene-canvas" class="clip" data-start="0" data-duration="<sec>" data-track-index="0" data-layout-allow-overflow="true" width="1080" height="1920"></canvas>

timeline_sync: Register window.__timelines["main"] = tl (GSAP paused timeline) after tweens.
Also listen to window.addEventListener("hf-seek", (e) => renderAt(e.detail.time)) for deterministic frame seeking.
No Date.now(), unseeded Math.random(), network fetches inside render loop, timers, or repeat: -1.
Never call play(), pause(), or seek on <audio>/<video>.
pre_render_validation: Run `npx hyperframes@0.9.47 check --json` and ensure ok=true and 0 errors across lint, runtime, layout, contrast, and audio.
Run `npx hyperframes@0.9.47 snapshot --at <timestamps>` and inspect contact-sheet.jpg to verify no black or clipped frames.

performance_findings: preserveDrawingBuffer: true is mandatory so HyperFrames beginFrame/screenshot captures the WebGL canvas reliably.
Avoid full-res EffectComposer + UnrealBloomPass on 1080x1920 SwiftShader CPU rendering (causes ~1.1s/frame and 30+ min renders).
Direct renderer.render(scene, camera) with antialias: false and 512x512 PCFShadowMap renders 3-5x faster while keeping 1080x1920 crisp.
Always remove unused references (e.g., leftover composer.render()) after refactoring renderer setup.

chunked_render_pipeline.why: 1750 frames (58.33s @ 30fps) at 1080x1920 on CPU SwiftShader exceeds the 300s bash timeout in one shot.
strategy: Render in 3.0s to 4.5s chunks (2.25s for heavy close-up scenes) using `--fps 30 --quality looks --workers 4 --start <t0> --end <t1> -o parts/part_XX.mp4` wrapped in `timeout 240`.

Concatenate video streams losslessly and mux original untouched audio: `ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i concat.txt -i assets/voice.mp3 -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
Extract decoded frames from out.mp4 with ffmpeg and inspect them visually before delivery.

audio_and_lipsync.rule: Keep original voice.mp3 intact (no background music or extra SFX unless requested); no subtitles when requested.
audio_and_lipsync.lipsync_generation: Decode voice.mp3 via ffmpeg to 24kHz mono s16le PCM, compute per-frame RMS amplitude at 30fps, write window.AUDIO_ENV + window.DIALOGUE to assets/lipsync.js.

github_delivery_and_token_efficiency.github_upload: Use GitHub REST API PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} with base64-encoded content (works for files <100 MB; include existing file sha when updating). Never print tokens in stdout/logs.
token_optimization: Start a fresh session once the architecture is decided instead of carrying 200k+ tokens of old logs/images across 20+ render calls.
Use quiet/filtered CLI flags (jq, tail -n 20) so verbose logs do not bloat conversation history.
